customize.name: Capybara
customize.desc:
These herbivores, which often dwell close to the water, are famous for their steely, stoic "won't even twitch if lightning strikes right next to their toes" disposition. Tourists consider them to be the paragon of animal friends.
Capybaras like to zone out while having a soak in the water, or sun themselves on the shore, and it's quite common for them to barely move for most of the day, as though not a single thing in the world could possibly perturb their calm demeanor and make them anxious. Despite their fluffy appearance, their hairs are actually quite hard and tough. If you pet them in the same direction as their coat of hair, it feels relatively smooth, but should you pet them in the opposite direction, you may end up with a scratched hand. Perhaps that is the reason even famished predators do not regard these completely harmless and quite defenseless little friends as prey...

"Scions of the Canopy"

Coatepec Mountain is home to the Scions of the Canopy tribe, whose buildings are suspended on the cliffsides. The Scions of the Canopy are renowned for their extreme sports: Free Solo Climbing, Mountain Parkour, Hot Air Balloon Racing, Cliff Bungee Jumping, and much more. Because all tribe members are specially trained, tourists are prohibited from participating in these sports at any time of day without training, instruction, special equipment, and supervision. Despite these precautions, tourists often fall from the cliff face and are rescued by Yumkasaurs, expending incredible amounts of effort.

The Scions of the Canopy's chief is Wayna, whose mantra is, <color=#ffffffd9>"Life isn't complete without taking risks."</color> Some tribe members call him "Uncle," but in reality, he is quite young, and maturity simply means extensive adventure experience. When one of the Night Warden Wars' participants, Kachina of the Children of Echoes, was not resurrected by the Ode of Resurrection, her friends and crew approached Wayna, asking to borrow the Spiritspeaker Stone, an artifact created by a great shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind that allows one to find an Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. Although Wayna knew that traveling into the night realm was fraught with danger, he agreed to lend the artifact. During the ritual, the Abyss's corruption attempted to escape from the Night Kingdom, and the Spiritspeaker Stone had to be destroyed to stop it. The hero of the tribe, Vichama, aided in the search for the Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. He later died during the Abyss's invasion, and a memorial can now be found in the place Vichama frequented.

One of the main attractions of the tribe's settlement is the Obsidian Totem Pole of the Scions of the Canopy, a legendary relic said to be connected with the tribe's Wayob and able to hear people's wishes. The Scions of the Canopy believe their Wayob has the power to control the growth of fruits and leaves, and can also control the roots of crops and draw the patterns of the veins of leaves. Legend has it that the warriors of the tribe, along with one hundred Yumkasaurs, spent a hundred days and a hundred ropes moving the "Obsidian Totem Pole," the symbol of their faith, to its current location. Currently, this relic is under the watchful eye of Accla, who can provide orders for monsters or supplies to enhance the tribe's reputation. In addition to guarding the Totem Pole, Accla also treats the Saurians' wounds.

Due to their passion for extreme sports and their connection with the Yumkasaurs, members of the Scions of the Canopy are excellent couriers in both peacetime and wartime. They were the ones who delivered reports from the front during the Abyss's attack. In the Scions of the Canopy settlement, the Courier's Longhouse, run by Michica, can be found. He accepts delivery orders and hires couriers, and often encounters smuggling in his work. Michica is also a certified player of Genius Invokation TCG. The office's employees send letters and packages not only between tribes but also to other nations. To do so, they must submit a request to the chieftain. However, correspondence to other nations is often delivered to the borders of Natlan and then handed over to foreign postmen. Every month, the Courier's Longhouse compiles a ranking of courier achievements and collects equipment evaluation reports. Since couriers often spend their rewards on high-quality equipment, the tribe strives to listen to all their wishes and concerns. Not far from the representative office, another Genius Invokation TCG player, the warrior Pacha, who dreams of making friends with the Riders of the Flower-Feather Clan, can be met. In addition, at the foot of the mountain and near the tribe's settlement, lost parcels can be found, which Michica can be contacted about.

On the upper level of the settlement is the home of the tribe elder, Trinidad, and his daughter, Huni. One day, Trinidad's Yumkasaurus, Nanna, was injured by the Abyss, leaving behind three Yumkasaurus whelps. To bring them back to the tribe, Huni and her friend secretly escaped from home, but along the way, they encountered a strange outlander who introduced himself as
He began questioning them about the tribe's history, including the history of the Turnfire, and promised to send his friends to search for the Yumkasaurs. When the Traveler and Paimon passed by the Scions of the Canopy's settlement, Enjou had already fled, and the children mistook them for helpers. During their search, they encountered Ajaw, a companion of the tribe's hero, Kinich, who told them how Nanna had fallen under the influence of the Abyss and attacked her offspring before jumping off a cliff. It later turned out that Nanna had fallen on Enjou, who was passing by the settlement. He assumed the Saurian was bungee jumping. The courage it took to make the jump amazed him to the core, so he befriended the Yumkasaurus and helped tend to her wounds. As a sign of their meeting, he even drew a picture of the ancient ruins, which was taken as a relic of the ancient Saurians. When Sanka finally escaped from the Traveler and Kinich, he was reunited with his friend and found that all of her wounds had healed. She missed her family very much, and Sanka took her to Huni, who told him the story of the Turnfire.

Various shops are located on the lower level of the settlement. One of them is Amauta's, which makes extreme sports equipment and souvenir clothing for tourists. The shop uses the finest ore from the Children of Echoes, fabrics from the Collective of Plenty, and foreign materials. Amauta also repairs sports equipment for the tribe. Traveling merchants selling obsidian can sometimes be found at the marketplace. All obsidian in Natlan is mined and sold by the Children of Echoes, with only a few merchants selling it outside the tribe.

At the foot of Coatepec Mountain, beneath the main settlement, a tribal secret space can be found. Three green obsidian fragments, obtained from Luxurious or Precious chests throughout the Scions of the Canopy, combined into a ring, are needed to open it. While traveling through Natlan with their Saurian companion, Little One, the Traveler and Paimon discovered an unconscious man, knocked down by a Tepetlisaurus, north of Coatepec Mountain. He was surrounded by three Saurians: a Tepetlisaurus, a Koholasaurus, and a Yumkasaurus. When the Traveler and Paimon rushed to the man's aid, the Saurians refused to let them in. They decided to explore the area to learn more. Nearby, they discovered the man's journal, in which he wrote about the Saurians. The Koholasaurus, Ripple, loved Sour Sauce Kipper, the Yumkasaurus, Jade, loved to play, and the Tepetlisaur, Marigold, was actually kind and tender. To distract the Saurians, the Traveler and Paimon asked Little One to lead Jade to play away, cooked Ripple some Sour Sauce Kipper, and defeated Marigold in combat when she refused to negotiate. When the man awoke, he introduced himself as the adventurer named Icayo. Shortly before their meeting, he had suffered an illness and was bedridden, preventing him from meeting the Saurians. They surrounded Icayo before he even reached camp, and Marigold knocked him down, but the adventurer still believed the Saurians were looking out for him.

Southwest of the settlement, a totem pole leading to the Night Kingdom can be found. In the Night Kingdom, a spirit of Cihuacoatl of Chimeric Bone can be dueled.

customize.text: Teticpac Peak

Teticpac Peak lies south of the Scions of the Canopy's settlement. At the peak, sacred flame offshoots, which the tribesmen requested from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, are located. These flames contain the power of the Pyro Archon. The Scions of the Canopy required them to perform a Turnfire Night, a traditional ceremony in which they remember their ancestor, Malipo Burkina, and his companion, the Mountain King Kongamato. They lived five hundred years ago and fought together against the Abyss, but victory came at a high price. The Mountain King was corrupted by the Abyss and attacked Burkina, then fell into hibernation. Every year, the unstable Abyssal energy within the Yumkasaurus awakened him, causing him to attack anything that moved. Therefore, an important part of the annual Turnfire Night was the cleansing of the Abyssal energy within the Mountain King so that he could continue his slumber. As Abyss-related incidents in Natlan increased, the Mountain King's sleep became increasingly difficult to maintain, and five months after the previous ceremony, he again showed signs of restlessness. Since the Scions of the Canopy's flame bearer, Kinich, only agreed to perform the ceremony for an additional fee, the tribal elder, Trinidad, requested the assistance of the Traveler and Paimon as Kinich's acquaintances.

A Turnfire Night ceremony consisted of several parts. First, the flame bearer had to collect a kindling of the Sacred Flame from the starting point, then use a grappling hook to fly up into the sky and light each of the Sacred Flame Pillars. Then, they had to go down into the canyon in Tequemecan Valley, all the way to the cave where the Mountain King slumbered, lighting braziers and the final altar along the way. The most skilled flame bearers could accomplish all of this without touching the ground once, but the main rule was never to look back, no matter what. To prepare the Traveler for the ceremony, Trinidad staged a training session at Teticpac Peak, in which the Traveler had to receive the protection of the Sacred Flame from the braziers and dispel the energy of the Abyss.

After training, the Traveler and Paimon met Kinich, who believed that Trinidad wanted not only to cleanse the Mountain King's Abyssal energy and put him to slumber, but to completely dispel it and send the symbol of the Scions of the Canopy to the Night Kingdom. Kinich proposed a deal whereby the Traveler and Paimon would continue to feign agreement with Trinidad's plan but would ensure the Mountain King's safety. The tribe's chief, Wayna, also agreed with Kinich's plan, as the roots of the tribe's identity were at stake. While hunting the Abyss, he pursued the Rifthounds and entered the space from which they emerged. If such a Rift were cleared of monsters and the Mountain King were placed within, he could continue to live, posing no threat to humans or Saurians. While hunting the Abyss, Kinich discovered not only the Rifthounds but also Enjou, a member of the Abyss Order, and took him into custody. From Enjou, Kinich obtained a special device capable of stabilizing the Abyss and luring the Rifthounds to open an entrance to the space. In exchange, Kinich allowed him to conduct historical research.

During the ceremony, Kinich attempted to open the Rift, but Trinidad broke the device and stood before the altar of the Sacred Flame, seeking to prove through his sacrifice the necessity of killing the Mountain King. Thanks to Kinich's intervention, Kongamato remembered his old friend and the oath he had sworn. He was able to awaken the Turnfire's powers, which created a protective shell around him, preventing the Abyss from harming him or those around him.

Near the ceremonial Sacred Flame offshoots, to the west of Coatepec Mountain, a mechanism that looks like a windmill can be found. After activating it to match the wind blades with the image on the stones, one of the six Broken, Graffiti-Marked Stones needed to complete the graffiti in the cave beneath the mountain can be obtained.

At Teticpac Peak lies the ruins of an ancient civilization that existed even before the first Pyro Archon. Near these ruins, a strange mural can be found, which one of the tribe members, Thiago, mistook for an ancient Saurian relic. He believed it depicted a Saurian and a human participating in some kind of Saurian-era pact ritual. Thiago wanted to take a photo of the mural to submit to the Saurian Relic Association, but the area was overrun by Abyssal monsters. The Traveler and Paimon agreed to help him and set out for the ancient ruins, but it later turned out that the image had been left by Enjou after meeting the Saurian Nanna.

When the Traveler and Paimon returned to Thiago with the photo of the mural, they encountered another member of the Scions of the Canopy, whose work, "Yupanqui's Turnfire," had been stolen by a Treasure Hoarder. When the Traveler and Paimon caught up with the thief, he had already disposed of the researcher's belongings, finding no Mora within them. In the cave beneath Coatepec Mountain, where the Treasure Hoarder had abandoned the book, Kinich and his companion, Ajaw, imprisoned Enjou, who was trying to learn about the Turnfire and the Dragonlord, Ajaw. From the book, Enjou learned that all bearers of the Ancient Name Malipo had died violent deaths, so he offered Ajaw a deal to take Kinich's body. However, their deal fell through, as Kinich presented Enjou as a "gift" to the Traveler, and the member of the Abyss Order fled, as usual.

In the cave where Kinich attempted to open the Rift with Enjou's device, a strange Yumkasaurus can be encountered, guarding the entrance to the treasure. To get rich, his companion deceived many people during his work as a courier, using trusted information. When the truth came to light, he lost his job and later fell ill. His Saurian companion stayed with him through it all. Realizing he couldn't survive for long, the courier left a note in an empty chest and told the Yumkasaurus to guard it, hoping that should the chest grab the attention of kind passersby, they might feed the Saurian. After the Traveler, Paimon, and their companion fed the Yumkasaurus and read the note from the chest, they approached Chief Wayna, who promised to feed the Saurian regularly as a member of their tribe.
In the same cave is a wall with unfinished graffiti. After collecting all Broken, Graffiti-Marked Stones and completing the drawing, the wall disappears, revealing the treasure.

South of Teticpac Peak is a shallow beach and a dock where people can fish. Passing by, Paimon wanted to cook some fish for her and the Traveler's Saurian companion, but while fishing, she caught a bottle attached to a plank. The note contained a message from two people, arranging to meet at their usual fishing spot. However, one of the friends, due to old age, had begun to forget his way home and had to ask people to bring his other friend for help. After several unsuccessful attempts, the Traveler and Paimon finally managed to catch some fish and fry them for dinner.

Not far from the pier, in the southern part of the location, the Traveler and Paimon once encountered a strange man counting stones. He believed he had discovered a special treasure stone that could breathe. If fed smaller stones, it would produce even more beautiful ones. The man asked the Traveler for some, and Paimon brought him stones, including Trishiraite, which can only be found in the Sumeru Desert. The next day, when they returned to check on the man and the stone, the man was nowhere to be found, and the stone turned out to be an Avatar of Lava.

To the northeast of Teticpac Peak is a camp where the Traveler, Paimon, and their Saurian companion spotted a wounded Qucusaurus and warriors surrounding it. After the Traveler drove off the warriors, the Tepetlisaurus led them to a nearby Embercore Flower, which filled the wounded Ququsaurus with phlogiston and allowed it to return home. East of the camp, a Broken, Graffiti-Marked Stone can be found.

North of the peak is a small, abandoned, dry field, where the Traveler and Paimon's Tepetlisaurus companion discovered a plant seed. Not to upset Little One, they planted the seed and attempted to awaken it with phlogiston, but this only attracted phlogiston aphids and monsters. After defeating the monsters and deciding that the plant might need time to grow, the Traveler and Paimon returned a few days later to find Embercore Flowers growing in the field.

Not far from this field are ancient dragon ruins. Legend has it that in ancient times, the colossal beasts that roamed the land had a civilization of their own. After exploring the entirety of the land and surrounding sea, they built these structures in an attempt to cast their gaze upon the even wider world beyond. At that time, the great dragon's outstretched wings could together blot out the light of the sky. Perhaps such descriptions were not hyperbole, or perhaps such wording was a metaphor for their desire to see beyond the sky. But now, the traces of said ancient dragon have already vanished, and the people of today can only glimpse the forging techniques of that ancient civilization through the shattered remnants of those massive structures and their patterns.

To the northeast of Teticpac Peak, another ruin from the time of the dragons can be found. There was once a time when people had yet to attain true mastery of the flames, there were sages in all corners of the world who pondered the fire and sought to fathom its mysteries. It is said that these ruins are all that is left of what was once a ring-shaped ceremonial site. Here, these sages attempted to perfect the rituals required to transform phlogiston. Among the heroes who later followed the first Pyro Archon into the belly of the volcano, there were several who once trained in this place.

Near the ruins, you can encounter a lutenist from the People of the Springs, Sappho Amidst the Waves. She is a friend of the flutist from the Masters of the Night-Wind, Rilay, and they often correspond, discussing their musical compositions. In a cave beneath the ruins, a totem pole leading to the Night Kingdom, where you can battle the "Atlatl's Blessing," can be found.

the people of that ancient era turned to the gods of night for guidance. They prayed for a revelation that would alter the course of all things. The people built a temple on Coatepec Mountain, where they brought offerings to the
The Natlanese ancestors plundered the barbarians who served the ancient dragons, destroyed their idols, and sprinkled the earth with the blood of their captives as an offering.

<color=#ffffffd9>"...offer to the Lord of the Crossroads... offer to the Father in Black... when the ears of grain wave like a sea, when the flowers are in bloom, when the canals are in full flow..."</color>

However, the sacrifices of the Natlanese ancestors were rejected, and the Lord of the Crossroads spoke of the approach of a
The white earth spread, and soon, the regions surrounding the temple were swallowed by the wastelands. The refugees could no longer offer grain to the gods of the night, the warriors of each region's leader were reduced to exile, and soon, all the tribes once again became barbarians serving the dragons. Years later, when the dragons were defeated and the Scions of the Canopy settled on Coatepec Mountain, they reestablished contact with the Night Kingdom in the Ancestral Temple using a medium, an ancient relic used by humans to communicate with the Wayob, the envoys of the Night Kingdom. From then on, many members of the tribe were able to enter the Night Kingdom's gates, and over time, they no longer needed the medium, but it remained an important relic of the tribe.

One day, the Traveler, Paimon, and their Saurian companion were wandering near the Ancestral Temple and discovered three Courier's Trial Keystones, stone mechanisms used to unlock the gates of ancient altars. Legba explained the history of the temple and that his territory was forbidden for outsiders, then invited them to stay in his camp for the night. That night, the Traveler was awakened by Little One, who brought a medium from the temple. Although the obsidian relic hadn't been used in a long time, Legba ordered for it to be returned to avoid the Wayob's wrath.

After opening the Ancestral Temple with the recovered Keystones, the Traveler, Paimon, Little One, and Legba proceeded inside, but their path to the altar was blocked by various trials and a flooded space. When the water in the hall was lowered using mechanisms, they were met by an angered Wayob Manifestation near the altar. As the Traveler and Paimon were about to return the medium, they were suddenly teleported to the Night Kingdom. A gentle voice called to them through the obsidian statue in their hands, warning them of the Abyss's invasion and the need to reject the promise of the Sage of the Stolen Flame.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Long has it been since visitors from afar have come. This place is... too big. Too empty.</color>

Vasily, Sidorenko, and Nomonkonov, who had been a technical specialist before joining the Fatui, worked at this center. For their research, the Fatui captured Saurians and extracted phlogiston from them for study. When the Traveler, Paimon, and their Saurian companion discovered the center, they freed all the captured Saurians and defeated the Fatui agents. More than six thousand years ago, a
appeared in Teyvat and declared war on the elemental dragons, the rulers of that world. When the dragons were defeated, the Heavenly Principles created humans and reshaped Teyvat to accommodate them. Angels were also created, heavenly envoys who guided and instructed human civilizations. After the dragons were defeated, the Dragon King, Nibelung, traveled beyond the world's borders to obtain
seeing it as salvation. When Nibelung returned, a new war broke out, during which Natlan's Ley Lines were damaged. In this war, the angels were devoured by the awakened dragons, the
of Natlan was burned by the Dragon King's flames, and humanity plunged into savagery, losing the ability to perceive the world anew. They reverted to their most primal beliefs, convinced of the inherent mystery of the earth that nurtured all things. This marked the dawn of the era where hunted prey began to be offered as sacrifices.

Only a few angels remained in Natlan. They rallied around Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, and offered their power to humanity to restore the Ley Lines. The Lord of the Night witnessed the people's resolute desire to survive and became their faith. People began praying to the gods of the night and making sacrifices to them. To help the Natlanese, the angel used fragments of the old Ley Lines to recreate a similar network. Thus, the Night Kingdom was created, a mysterious, liminal space between the body and mind, life and death, where the souls of all the dead Natlanese go. One of the shades of the Heavenly Principles, the
helped the angel create the Night Kingdom, she wanted to compensate for the damage and express her love for the people.

During the ancient war between the Descenders and the dragons, damaged Ley Lines allowed the Abyss to penetrate Teyvat and the Night Kingdom. Gradually, the Lord of the Night began to weaken, and the Cataclysm, which occurred five hundred years ago and during which the Abyss invaded Teyvat again, almost completely destroyed the Ley Lines. After the Cataclysm, the Natlanese calculated that no more than five centuries remained until the complete dissolution of the Night Kingdom in the Abyss, but then Natlan lay in ruins. The Pyro Archon, Mavuika, decided to give the tribes time to rebuild the land so that they would be ready for the last battle. She entered the Sacred Flame to be reborn when Natlan's time was running out.

Five hundred years later, the Night Kingdom was nearly absorbed by the Abyss, and the Lord of the Night had fallen into slumber to prolong her existence. The Fatui Harbinger Capitano, distrusting Mavuika's plan, decided to restore the Natlan's Ley Lines by his own means. He utilized the Source Mechanism of the ancient dragons hidden beneath Coatepec Mountain. The ancient dragons tried to use this device to strengthen the Ley Lines by imbuing them with power, but they lacked the skills to navigate the intricate structure of the Ley Lines. Restoring the Ley Lines in this way would destroy all memory stored within them, so Capitano was stopped. When the Source Mechanism was activated, the Night Lord was awakened by it, and she was able to absorb some of that power to help the Natlanese once again.

To fulfil her plan, the Pyro Archon used the power of the Ruler of Death to destroy the Abyss in Natlan, but the price for this power was death. Mavuika was willing to give her life in exchange for the restoration of the Ley Lines. The Archon's life force would have to be enough to keep the Flame going for another two or three centuries, during which time the next Pyro Archon would have to find new sources. But another man approached the angel with a similar proposal, Captaino, a Khaenri'ahn cursed with immortality from the nation that had caused the Cataclysm. Thanks to the Khaenri'ahn technologies, his heart was able to convert memories and souls from the Ley Lines into knowledge. A side effect was a high sensitivity to souls, and after the Cataclysm, he began to use his heart as a vessel for lost souls. Since then, Capitano has held the lives of his comrades and the lives of many Natlanese in his heart. By becoming one with the Lord of the Night, he could change the laws that govern the Night Kingdom and allow the souls within his heart to find peace. Yohualtecuhtin knew that with Captaino's immortality, the Night Kingdom could exist forever, and so she agreed to his proposal.

Since the Ruler of Death could not lift the curse of immortality from Capitano, she was forced to forgo the price of her power, and Capitano merged with the Lord of the Night. The legends of the Natlanese ancestors dedicated to the Lord of the Crossroads say that he was both the black-robed "Papa Witch Doctor" and "Mama Dream-Realm" all rolled into one. And it was to him that they prayed, hoping for a revelation that could change everything.

customize.text: Sage of the Stolen Flame

Long before the existence of humanity, Teyvat was ruled by a highly advanced dragon civilization led by the primordial dragon, Nibelung. On the land that would be called Natlan thousands of years later, on the Sacred Mountain, the first Pyro Sovereign, Xiuhcoatl, was born from the primal fire, founded the Sacred City of Tollan, and created the Dragonborn with the primal fire. He gave his first creation, his brother Kukulkan, a piece of that same fire, which the descendants of the dragons considered part of a great soul. When the reaver from beyond the skies appeared in Teyvat, a war began between the First Descender and the dragons, during which the reaver froze Xiuhcoatl in lava, causing him to fall into a false death. When Nibelung returned to Teyvat with the forbidden knowledge, the Flamelord was called forth by the Abyss and awoke from his long dream. The reaver annihilated the Dragon King at great cost, and at that moment, the Flamelord, who had been steeped in the Abyss, regained brief, tragic clarity.

To fight the reavers and the Abyss, in the moments of clarity, Xiuhcoatl decided to use a weapon capable of transforming all of Natlan into a land consisting only of phlogiston matter. All life would either be destroyed or forced to abandon its body and become phlogiston-based life forms. Then the dragons, now phlogiston-based life forms, would rule this new world. Although the dragon court, blindly following their ruler, agreed to this plan, Kukulkan was horrified. All life, transformed into flickering, illusory shadows cast by a giant torch, would be deprived of any chance to evolve. Kukulkan knew that the Flamelord, who had experimented on himself for Huitzilopochtli's creation, would be the first to die from the use of this power, so he did not agree to his brother's plan. He saw light fall upon the rootless earth, dragons prostrating before their ruler's deathbed, a great civilization perished, and the world obeyed cycles. The sage of the dragons knew that the gods in the heavens and the king of all dragons lacked the power to defeat the enemies hiding in the deepest corners of the Night Kingdom. He hoped that in the abundant primordial wilderness, there was a land that wasn't touched by filth and decay.

Appointed regent after Xiuhcoatl's corruption, the wisest of dragons decided to find another solution and go to humans, in whom he saw the hope of evolution. Humans were the most beloved and weakest creations of the Heavenly Principles, who had taken the place of dragons. According to the legend, Kukulkan passed through searing flame and raging wind and took unextinguished
from the ancient palace beneath the magma, becoming the Sage of the Stolen Flame. The wisest among dragons traversed the burning plains, carrying the seed split from the primal flame, stepping into a rugged, untamed land. He walked through hot springs and valleys that dragonkind had yet to touch, and one day, the fog dispersed in a deep valley, and humans appeared before him. These creatures, who should still have been wrapped in swaddling cloths, yet were born in a land where dragons did dance, could survive only in the shadow of ancient wings.

Although they had long lost their guide, forgotten their past histories and memories, and lost themselves amidst mountains and woods, they survived. Marveling at their tenacity, unity, and courage, the sage among dragons resolved to grant them the flaming seed of wisdom. But that gift had its price: it would civilize these barbarians, but it would also order their destinies, and unlike the plan of that first divine one, what the most sage one brought was the profane path of "evolution." Kukulkan foresaw that at the end of this path, human blood would be poured, two species, two bloodlines, would merge as one, and an ancient pulse would surge through a reborn civilization.

Among the people, the Sage of the Stolen Flame met Chaac. The brave and wise Chaac took the ever-bright kindling from the hands of the wisest of the dragons and shared this kindling with his fellow tribespeople, passing the secret of fire on to all who came forth to study it. Thus, the new sprouts of civilization sprang up once more from the untamed wilderness. After mastering the majestic primal flame, fearless Chaac and his companions founded the first tribe.
According to legend, when the Sage of the Stolen Flame shared the seed of fire with the people, they imitated the dragons, creating a language to control phlogiston. This is how Phlogiston Engravings were born. In ancient times, there was a sage who attained such mastery of the art of Phlogiston Engraving that they could transform all its many meanings into graceful, drifting lines. With phlogiston as their medium, they used towering cliffs as canvases for vibrant murals. This, it is said, is the origin of Natlan graffiti as we know it now.

customize.text: Qoyllor and Ukuku

According to legend, long, long ago, a bright star, where Qoyllor lived, shone in the sky. This star was closest to the ground, yet still she was inestimably far away from her brothers and sisters. Her father, the Sun, bestowed upon her power, which he commanded her to cherish. Just as people on the ground gaze up in awe at the starry sky, she often looked down upon the life of the tribes in Natlan. One day, she leaned too far forward and accidentally fell from the sky. Falling to the ground, the star lost its former brilliance, and her power shattered into fragments that were scattered across the land. Without it, Qoyllor could no longer return to the sky. Life on the ground had previously seemed so curious and fascinating to her, but when she descended and lost the chance to return home, her heart became heavy.
For a long time, Qoyllor wandered Natlan in search of the fragments of her star, facing many dangers, but all her searches were in vain. One day, by utter chance, she encountered the fierce warrior and hunter, Ukuku, strong and silent as a bear. Upon learning of her plight, he agreed to help her search for the scattered shards of her star so she could return. Together, they set off on their roamings: they climbed high mountains and ventured into deep ravines, overcoming hordes of enemies and making scores of friends. Gradually, Qoyllor adapted to life on the ground and became a true Natlanese. Like humans, she hunted, fought, rested with the Saurians, and told children wonderful stories. And only at night, unlit by glowing graffiti, did she suddenly remember her homeland and her brothers and sisters.

After years of fruitless searching, Qoyllor decided that, in the same way that she had become a part of the tribe, her lost power had long since been found. She asked Ukuku if he had grown tired of chasing such an elusive goal, but the only answer he gave was a short <color=#ffffffd9>"Sorry."</color> She didn't understand why the hunter was apologizing, as he had always been kind to her, and from the very beginning of their search, they had found no clue about the lost power. Qoyllor and Ukuku were to form a family together, settling down in a corner of the tribe. Qoyllor's home was so far away, but at night the twinkling stars seemed to greet her as if they were her brothers and sisters themselves, and she was happy. But the silent Ukuku became even more gloomy, as if something were tormenting him.
Ukuku had an envious and cunning neighbor, Pochica, who, from time to time, began speaking badly of Ukuku in front of Qoyllor, embellishing his stories with malicious barbs. He said she was like a bird that had had its wings clipped, locked in a cage. At first, Qoyllor paid no attention to this gossip, but over time, doubts began to creep into her heart. She didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing, so she tried to uncover the truth through playful remarks. Under the pressure of her questioning, Ukuku soon confessed that, in fact, he long ago found some star shards. But by that time, Ukuku had already developed feelings for her, so he decided not to give up the shards, to keep her on the ground.
After hearing Ukuku's confession, Qoyllor felt sadness and anger. She had never known deceit and betrayal before, but now she understood how deeply they hurt. She really was a bird whose wings had been clipped. Realizing she could never forgive Ukuku, Qoyllor demanded the star shards back, but he refused. The hunter believed that everything would work out between them. Ignoring his pleas, Qoyllor left the tribe she had once considered home and set out to wander again. Like a true person of Natlan, she left a huge work of graffiti on the vast expanse of land so that her Sun-father could see it from the sky. Qoyllor's father heard her plea, quickly bringing her back to the sky, and since then, the star that had lost its power became dim and was now almost invisible unless you looked very closely. Ukuku, who had been left behind, his deceit and betrayal angered the Sun. As punishment, he was blinded by the Sun's golden arrows. From then on, wherever he went, the Sun would retreat behind the clouds, leaving him without a trace of sunlight.

customize.text: The Abyss Invasion

During the war between the Descenders and the dragons, Natlan's Ley Lines were significantly damaged, and during the Cataclysm, they were almost completely destroyed, so the Abyss was not completely banished. For five hundred years, the Abyss grew in power by attacking the tribes. At first, the attacks seemed random, and the Abyss appeared to be a natural phenomenon, but it later turned out that the attacks occurred at the tribes' vulnerable points. Using memories stored in Natlan's Night Kingdom, the Abyss studied all the tribes' weaknesses, as if possessing a consciousness. And five hundred years after the Cataclysm, it launched a full-scale invasion of all the tribes of Natlan simultaneously.

Allied with the Fatui under the leadership of the Harbinger Capitano, the Natlanese rushed to defend their tribes. Since the Scions of the Canopy were renowned for their couriers, they traveled throughout Natlan with adventurers from the Guild to relay information about enemy advances. Near the tribe's main settlement, the warriors established a temporary shelter to provide safety for the wounded and those unable to move quickly. But when the outpost was attacked by the Abyss, they were forced to evacuate the residents to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and the tribe's main settlement.

East of Teticpac Peak, on the main trade route from the Children of Echoes to the People of the Springs, monsters attacked caravanners, and the Fatui rushed to their defense. At Capitano's orders, they placed themselves under the command of the Pyro Archon. Although not everyone understood the decision, the word of the Harbinger was law, and the Fatui were ready to sacrifice their lives to protect the people. Then, Capitano himself departed for the Ancestral Temple. Since the path to the People of the Springs was too dangerous, the Fatui went to the Stadium to strengthen the defenses near the Sacred Flame.

Despite all of Natlan's resistance, the Abyss Pylons, constantly creating monsters, appeared in ever-increasing numbers, and the Abyss itself used its main weapon: Gosoythoth. The immense energy of the Abyss took on an unimaginable form, looming over Natlan and casting a shadow over the entire sky. Many territories, including Teticapac Peak and the Ancestral Temple, were completely overrun by monsters, and all life there was destroyed. A temporary refuge near the Scions of the Canopy settlement was attacked by monsters again. Some warriors went to evacuate the civilians, but of those who remained, only one survived. Among the sheltering residents, only the elderly remained, who were forced to take up arms.

Over time, the entire territory of Coatepec Mountain became overrun by the Abyssal monsters. Chief Wayna called for the evacuation of the main settlement, but many people died in the battle. Among them was Vichama, who excelled at scouting and analyzing the battlefield. He once helped the Traveler and friends find the Ancient Name of a girl from the Children of Echoes, whom the Ode of Resurrection had failed to revive, in the Night Kingdom. During the Night Warden Wars five years ago, Vichama injured his leg and couldn't participate, and his team was unable to overcome the Abyss and perished. Among the dead was Vichama's close friend, with whom he had been inseparable. Afterward, Vichama fell into depression and blamed himself for everything. But the battle at the Scions of the Canopy settlement allowed him to fulfill his dream. He scouted the location and direction of the attacks, so Chief Wayna would have the safest way to evacuate. Vichama remained with the tribe until the very end, providing information for the future of his tribe and all of Natlan. He did not fear death, for he knew that in the Night Kingdom he would meet his friend again, and together they would witness the birth of a new Natlan. Besides Vichama, the tribe's courier, Wayta, and the adventurer Hunza also perished. The hero of the tribe, Kinich, was later appointed by the Pyro Archon to identify the dead from the remaining clues.

The Pyro Archon, Mavuika, had already witnessed a battle of similar magnitude five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm. Although the Natlanese at that time had managed to drive the Abyss into the depths of the Night Kingdom, they knew it would eventually erupt again. The Pyro Archon had a long and involved discussion with the heroes of each tribe, and finally came up with a five-hundred-year-long plan to save Natlan. During this time, the Archons and chiefs were to rebuild the tribes, and when the time came, the Wayob would again choose six heroes of Natlan with the Ancient Names of Xbalanque's companions.

In the present day, when all six heroes necessary for Mavuika's plan were recognized by their Ancient Names, she used their power and the power of the divine throne to banish the Abyss. This power helped destroy the previously invulnerable Abyss Tumors, and the Ode of Resurrection enabled the resurrection of all Natlanese who had perished after using this power. Thanks to the Natlanese's bravery, Coatepec Mountain and other tribes were recaptured, and Mavuika was able to attack Gosoythoth, forcing it to flee into the Night Kingdom.

desc.text:
"O guests from afar who have scaled mountains on your way, the Scions of the Canopy extend their greetings to you."
"This is the Bulletin Board for our tribe's affairs. May here you find the information you seek, as well as a path to the attainment of your hopes."

"The new Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame is about to begin! Scions of the Canopy, make some noise for the contestants representing our tribe!"
"Give it up for the 'Azure Darts,' our very own veteran couriers Amada and Isela, as well as the renowned 'Peakwind Hunter,' aka the inimitable Mixquic... Familiar faces that never let us down!"
"Mr. Kibangu, the 'Cliffside Crusader' himself, who has consistently achieved outstanding results, has boldly declared his intent to secure a spot in the Night Warden Wars!"
"And let's not forget our extraordinarily talented Saurian Hunter duo, Kinich and Ajaw!"
"As always, while the competition's on, all courier work will be scheduled in advance and shifts specially assigned to ensure that everyone can attend the matches..."

"Brothers, sisters, Scions of the Canopy. By now, word has surely reached you all: victory is ours!"
"Let us come together to celebrate this triumph and commemorate the sacrifice of those heroes who gave their lives. And remember, there's no need to go rushing off to the next adventure! We could all do with a good rest."

"Given the special nature of extreme sports, the Scions of the Canopy only offer these activities to visitors under specific conditions. Please refer to the rules for each activity—"
"Free Solo Climbing: Due to the specific lighting conditions over at the small cliff, this activity is only available from 10:00 to 18:00 daily."
"Mountain Parkour: Opening hours vary, depending on when the safety officers complete their course inspection, but are usually between 11:00 and 19:00."
"Well you wouldn't want to come crashing down because you'd slipped on a Quenepa Berry or something like that, would you?"

"Hot Air Balloon Racing: Open daily from 07:00 to 20:00, weather permitting and within the safe temperature range."
"Cliff Bungee Jumping: Hours vary depending on the time it takes to set up the ropes, protective gear, and get the Yumkasaur safety team in place. Please await notification from the supervisor, Pacha."
"Rescuing participants who have slipped can be an extremely demanding task, so the Yumkasaur safety team will occasionally need a lie-in. Thank you for your understanding..."

"The majority of our tribe's buildings are suspended on the cliffsides. We kindly ask all visitors to stay safe and avoid getting too close to the platform edges."
"Until you have undergone the proper training and passed all the basic tests, we advise against casually attempting extreme sports like the Scions of the Canopy."
"Even though you'd likely be rescued by one of our valiant Yumkasaurs, and thus avoid coming to any real harm, the impact and dizziness of coming to a sudden stop after a free-fall can still be somewhat overwhelming..."
"You might be left with your legs shaking, traumatized for weeks... So even though you came up the mountain on foot, you'll find yourself crawling back down on your knees."

"A new batch of courier relay outposts is currently under construction. We're on the lookout for seasoned adventurers with plenty of experience in camping and wilderness survival!"
"Additionally, utilizing the latest wood treatment techniques from the Collective of Plenty, we've designed a brand-new type of supply station."
"To assess how well the tribe's Yumkasaurs adapt to these new buildings, we may be moving them around more frequently in the near future, as well as possibly enlisting the help of a few new Saurian friends."
"Please rest assured, there is no need for any concern or worry!"

"Children of Huitztlan, hear my voice."
"The skies darken and the tainted currents flow ever closer."
"The path of the Turnfire is long and winding. How exacting is the price of rushing into danger?"
"But the value of friendship is such that a hero would risk all to retrieve their friends..."

"Today's fast-food menu for the Small Cliff climbing station has been updated—"
"Our all-new Forest of Color paper meal box is light, portable, and spill-resistant, making it the perfect choice for a satisfying meal during your extreme sports adventures!"
"Additionally, the Quenepa Berry Freeze, an all-time favorite of the Yumkasaurs, is back with a vengeance!"
"This time, we've made the sugar coating tougher to prevent it from being crushed before it even reaches the Yumkasaurs' mouths, keeping your hands from getting all sticky! Just please, make sure your kids don't get their hands on them — for Saurians only!"
"Kids that accidentally eat them might have trouble sleeping at night, and could experience other strange side-effects such as wishing they had Saurian tails!"

"...The hour to transcend your limits has come! The Natlan branch of the Adventurers' Guild is now recruiting new members!"
"Scions of the Canopy, you who possess the courage to navigate the high peaks and towering cliff faces, extreme sports prodigies of outstanding agility — the Adventurers' Guild needs you!"
"Sign up during the event to receive instant access to expert courses and detailed notes compiled by renowned adventurers, three sets of high-quality Guild-standard attire, and we'll even throw in a rookie adventurers' starter kit too!"
"For more details, please visit our branch headquarters over at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and speak with Branch Master Mansa..."

"This bulletin board will display notices from the Courier's Longhouse as well as other courier-related inquiries. If you have any queries, please contact the maintenance staff."
"If you're looking to hire a courier, please head over to the Courier's Longhouse and find the manager, Michica. We only accept commissions on a per-delivery basis, and do not currently offer our services for fixed periods."
"Please also note: Couriers should not be entrusted with the delivery of extremely valuable, fragile, or dangerous items."
"Though our couriers are highly skilled professionals, and you can rest assured that the vast majority of deliveries will arrive safely, we cannot guarantee against unforeseen accidents that may occur along the way..."
"In the past, certain customers have asked our couriers to deliver packages with the speed of a falcon, across distances exceeding the deserts of Sumeru, with no damage to the packaging whatsoever..."
"Among today's Scions of the Canopy, only Kinich might be capable of such a task, but sadly he doesn't work as a courier... Anyway, your understanding is greatly appreciated!"
"Roll up, roll up, this month's courier performance rankings are out! Star courier Adama, who's been busy preparing for the Pilgrimage, has fallen down to fifth place!"
"The champion's position has been seized by none other than his teammate Zeila, who completed an astonishing 110 long-distance deliveries in just twenty days!"
"Could it be that Zeila has been treating delivering letters and packages as a form of training!? Unbelievable stuff... I'm starting to feel bad for the opponents she'll be facing in the upcoming Pilgrimage!"
"Ranked second to tenth, in the following order, we have: Tundama, Sausa, Sibu... All these couriers will receive a cash prize, plus a special "Yum Yum Yumkasaur" Chew Stick that Aclla made from the finest quality Cacahuatl!"
"Other fellow couriers, don't lose heart! Keep up the great work — maybe next month, the award will be yours!"
"Now that Michica has submitted the assessment report to Chief Wayna, the bidding process for the next generation of couriers' standard issue gear is about to begin."
"As per usual, before finalizing the bidding requirements, we will first gather feedback from the couriers. We encourage you all to share your thoughts—"
"Let us know which parts of the protective gear are more prone to damage, where screws tend to fall out, and which materials are less resistant to corrosion from moisture and Gaseous Phlogiston... Also, which safety ropes have poor weight-to-durability ratios. The more detailed the feedback, the better."
"We are well aware that the current usage rate of the standard issue gear is not very high, so we are determined to improve it to ensure that the management fees you all contribute are put to better use!"
"Please don't hesitate to share as many suggestions as possible to let Miss Amauta know what you value the most!"
"To all couriers delivering to the Flower-Feather Clan: Please ensure that you drop off your deliveries BEFORE engaging in racing contests with members of the Flower-Feather Clan."
"Otherwise, not only will you most likely lose, given how skilled they are at gliding, but on top of that, you might also damage the contents of your packages. It's just not worth the risk!"

textualResearch.title: Scions of the Canopy General Message Board

desc.text:
"At Chief Wayna's suggestion, this community bulletin board has been repurposed to serve as a general message board. Aside from being a place to display important news concerning the tribe, feel free to leave any other messages here too."
"Both members of the Scions of the Canopy and visitors from outside the tribe are welcome to share feedback and requests at any time!"

"The safest and simplest of extreme sports you could imagine — perfect for beginners! Head over to the small cliff to experience the joys of climbing for yourself!"
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "How can something that safe even be called an extreme sport? Doesn't seem fun in the slightest. If this is what the rock climbing in Natlan's like, I might as well have just stayed at home and gone hiking on my own."
<color=#37ffff>Edited Advertisement</color> : "The most authentic and challenging of extreme sports you could imagine — perfect for those looking for a challenge! Head over to the small cliff to experience the joys of climbing for yourself!"

"Our shop handles custom orders for all types of extreme sports gear as well as souvenir clothing for tourists!"
"In addition to fine ores supplied by the Children of Echoes and fabrics chosen by the Collective of Plenty, we also use various raw materials imported from abroad."
"Prices are negotiable, however big the order~"
<color=#37ffff>Advertisement Addendum</color> : "Important note: When ordering custom grappling hooks, please provide accurate body weight measurements. No shame in a few extra pounds — as long as a Yumkasaur can still lift you, you're good!"
<color=#37ffff>Advertisement Addendum</color> : "Accurate weight measurements are crucial for grappling hook safety!"

<color=#37ffff>Sinchi's Message</color> : "If you need anything brought back, feel free to leave a message below. As long as it's within my abilities, I'll find a way to bring it back."
<color=#37ffff>Childish Handwriting</color> : "You wouldn't be able to bring back some meat for me, would you, Sinchi? I want to make some food for my sick little Saurian!"
<color=#37ffff>Sinchi's Message</color> : "No problem, I'll bring it back for you tomorrow."
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "I want some chocolate, Sinchi!"
<color=#37ffff>Another Person's Message</color> : "Me too! Bring back some for me too!"
<color=#37ffff>Sinchi's Message</color> : "Hey now, it's not like Cacahuatl grows on trees, you know. Just reach down underground and dig some up for yourself!"

"This month, there were a total of eleven incidents. Nine involved damage to property and goods, and two resulted in injuries to travelers and personnel."
"Both travelers and new couriers — please, always exercise caution. Avoid reckless modes of travel, choose suitable paths and climbing routes, and prioritize your safety at all times."
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "Alright, alright, Uncle Wayna. You've told me this umpteen times already."
<color=#37ffff>Reply</color> : "Mayta, you little rascal! Just because you haven't gotten hurt yet, doesn't mean it doesn't apply to you... You of all people should be extra careful!"
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "No way! You have to take a few tumbles if you wanna get better, hehe!"

"...A gentle reminder from Aclla: When you're making friends with Yumkasaurs, make sure you adjust your approach depending on their age!"
"Generally speaking, both juvenile and adult Yumkasaurs enjoy having their noses — the part that protrudes above their mouth — gently pressed by their companions. A bit like how friends might give each other a friendly pat on the back."
"If you've got a baby Yumkasaur on your hands, they'll love a gentle ear rub."
"Some Yumkasaurs approaching adulthood may be sensitive about people touching their ears. After all, they're no longer little kids anymore — in their own minds, anyway!"
"Many little Yumkasaurs dislike it when other people groom their tails, for as their parents tell them, 'Little Saurians must grow up quickly and take care of themselves.'"
"Adult Yumkasaurs, on the other hand, particularly enjoy having their tails groomed, as they love showing off how well-kept their fur is..."
"A bit like a hairdresser telling you, 'Your hair's so thick and lush — must be hard trying to manage it all on your own!'"
…

(A damaged stone tablet. The inscription on it has been eroded by the relentless passage of time, but you can still manage to vaguely make out some of what the remaining text says...)
"...offer to the Lord of the Crossroads... offer to the Guardian of the Land of Night... When the obsidian mirror is bathed in twilight..."
"...deity awaiting the decaying night's dreams... the envoy who accepts us... She will show us the ancient dream..."

(A damaged stone tablet. The inscription on it has been eroded by the relentless passage of time, but you can still manage to vaguely make out some of what the remaining text says...)
"...Thirty sacks of grain, thirty sacks of fruit, exchanged for copper ingots and obsidian of the same value... quality to be determined by the priests... oversee..."
"...on the day of the third lunar eclipse, the chief priest of the palace... dispatched shamans to each of the tribes, to collect funds for the poor as follows... payments are as follows... the duty scribe must make a record of..."
"...on the day of the third lunar eclipse, the chief priest sent the priests to the leaders of all the tribes of every region, to quell all conflict and ceremonial war, during which the sacrifice of prisoners of war shall be illegal, without exception..."

(A damaged stone tablet. The inscription on it has been eroded by the relentless passage of time, but you can still manage to vaguely make out some of what the remaining text says...)
"...offer to the Lord of the Crossroads... offer to the Father in Black... when the ears of grain wave like a sea, when the flowers are in bloom, when the canals are in full flow..."
"...The blood of heroes, the heads of nobles, the first cry of the newborn... We offer them to you, the Keykeeper of Countless Secrets, the Great Spirit that dwells deep within the dreamscape..."
"...all to seek from you the answers to our questions, to seek from you guidance on the path forward..."

(A damaged stone tablet. The inscription on it has been eroded by the relentless passage of time, but you can still manage to vaguely make out some of what the remaining text says...)
"...Thrice were all the barbarians who worshipped the evil dragons sacked, seizing... 'Relaxation Ravine,' and 'Twisted Ivy Expanse,' these three regions, uncounted ancient dragon idols destroyed, prisoners of war... all..."
"...chief priest... asked the Lord of the Crossroads... sprinkle the Essence of Sacrifice onto the soil, and each of the Head Elders of the three districts, of each of the tribes..."
"...priests of all tribes must recruit large numbers of craftsmen to expand the temples and forts, spreading their blessings to the savage lands once ruled by dragons..."

(A damaged stone tablet. The inscription on it has been eroded by the relentless passage of time, but you can still manage to vaguely make out some of what the remaining text says...)
"...The Lord of the Crossroads spake: 'The Great Spirit dreamed of the black tide'... The sacrifice was rejected..."
"...The white earth spreads, the six regions surrounding the temple swallowed by the wastelands... refugees could not offer grain..."
"...priests and elders alike were powerless, the warriors of each region's leader reduced to exile..."
"...the tribes of all regions, now are... and they have become barbarians once more.."

(There are pieces of paper scattered in the bottle. They seem to be messages between two people, one responding to the other. One person's handwriting is sloppy, and the other's script is composed.)
...
(Sloppy handwriting) "My dear friend! You-know-who in my household is being really strict, so I'll leave the fishing gear with you for now. Next time we go fishing, let's set up a time, and I'll make an excuse to sneak out. Remember! Do NOT come to the door and ask for me."

Yesterday, I even forgot the way home, and had to have someone ask you to come to the Golden Dusk and pick me up, after all, I can't let anyone in my family know about us fishing... Alas, people are so silly..."
(Composed handwriting) "So you really forgot the way, and it wasn't that you just wanted to show me the giant fish you caught, right?"
...
(Composed handwriting) "You really forgot the way, right?"

(The rest of the papers are soaked, and are completely illegible...)

(A seemingly incomplete musical composition is stuck within the notebook. The following is written below...)
Thanks for your suggestions. After making the adjustments, the musical inflections have indeed become more vivacious.
We haven't even met again since the last Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, have we?

textualResearch.title: Ancient Chronicle of the Dreamseeker Priest (II)

desc.text:
Angakuk, Angakuk.
Where will I hear that voice from beneath the earth...
Or a rumbling from even deeper underground. If you will it so, send forth an envoy.
Before dawn's first light, we shall take up arms to quell the Night Kingdom's unrest.
When I am ready, Angakuk, make your warrior manifest, Angakuk.

textualResearch.title: Ancient Chronicle of the Dreamseeker Priest (IV)

desc.text:
Angakuk, Angakuk.
Call forth the winds, then take both my hands, and with feverish fervor, let them pass through the gaps between the blazing flames.
If you can hear me, great Wayob, take my hands.
Then in them place the fruit, the ripened fruit, to serve as a testament!

(A maintenance log with an inspection report and evaluations for various machinery is attached.)
Transportation Pipe Heat Resistance: No issues.
Directional Valve: No issues.
Advance Drill: Brand new.
Friction Press: Functioning Perfectly.
...
Test results: No issues at all. It's quite surprising that the Fontaine Research Institute's equipment is in such good condition. I had thought that they would just chuck us some random gear to try and pull a fast one on us.

(This seems to be the diary of a soldier stationed here.)
...
I'm puzzled, to be honest. Why do we have to go to such lengths to capture Saurians from Natlan...
Something something phlogiston, special constitution, something something solid and liquid... Nomokonov seems more familiar with these things. I hear he had some kind of technical background before joining up with the Fatui.
He always tries to explain things to me, but it's all mumbo-jumbo to me. My brain just ain't cut out for that kinda stuff. The Fire-Water they sent us from Snezhnaya interests me more, anyway.
...
Our Lord has never revealed what all this phlogiston research is meant to be about.
That person from Natlan he brought with him the last couple of times seemed kinda suspicious, but we trust our Lord's judgment. Not like we care much about this stuff anyway...
First, a glass of Fire-Water, and then, sleep!
...
Note to self: Don't get locked inside next time.
I wish someone could've seen Vasily's face — he looked so pleased with himself, he did!
He's usually pretty likable, but so by-the-book when things need doing! Bo-ring.
Worse, there's no Fire-Water to drink today. Damn that Vasily, he took my stash!

textualResearch.title: Research Center Emergency Machine Operation Handbook

desc.text:
(A manual that seems to have seen a lot of use, judging by the proliferation of handwritten notes scrawled upon its pages.)
...
Regarding the Emergency Brake System:
The mining facility's brake system is a safety mechanism that must be manually activated and is designed to shut down the core and prevent mechanical damage resulting from malfunctions of the phlogiston research machinery.
When a potentially dangerous malfunction is detected, please activate the control consoles on both sides to initiate braking measures.
(Handwritten notes below...)
— Are these things they shipped us really all that useful? Is modifying it to be power it all with lava from Natlan even feasible...?
— Alright, Vasily, no point flipping through this manual any longer. Just keep your eye on these machines, humming and whirring away…
(Below this section is written...)
— Fine, as requested by Vasily, I hereby declare the following: I promise not to accidentally lock myself in the cage again, nor will I attempt to smash open the lock, thereby necessitating the activation of the braking system... On top of this, I solemnly swear that I will thoroughly read through this manual, cross my heart and hope to die. That's gotta be good enough, yeah?
— You'd better make good on that, Sidorenko. Seriously, if I have to catch those crazy little critters and put them all back in the cage one more time…

"...Today's a rainy day. I prepared "Ripple" his favorite <color=#37ffff>Sour Sauce Ceviche</color> . His look of satisfaction made it all worthwhile..."
"...Even if he's swimming in a leisurely manner, the moment I proffer some of that <color=#37ffff>Sour Sauce Ceviche</color> ... Whoosh! Out he pops from the water, and in such lovely form, too..."
"...I would never doubt his affection for me. Only, perhaps, that he might love <color=#37ffff>the ceviche</color> more..."
"...Big round sparkling eyes, curly tail and cheery cries... Jade, oh, Jade, is there a cuter Saurian in this world than you...?"
"...You have never once been cheated, nor never once doubted, as if all life might become your friend and enjoy a wonderful time playing with you..."
"...Were I not so busy, I'd love to play with you all day, watching you dart through woods swimming in mottled sunlight, like a child of the wind, a spirit oh so carefree..."

textualResearch.title: Note Left Inside a Treasure Chest

desc.text:
As of writing this note, I have already been laid low by serious illness. Alas, Wayob above, this too is my punishment.
To accumulate wealth, I took advantage of all the information I had access to as a courier and cheated many people.
In the end, after the incident happened, I lost my job as a courier, and all the Mora I swindled became restitution, and I even became gravely ill... Ah me, all I can say is that this punishment is agony... But even so, I still have things I can't get off my mind...
And that is the Yumkasaur who never left my side, my companion.
Alas, I do not have long to live.
I stole this chest. It is regrettable, but I had no choice... All I could do was have it guard this empty chest.
I hoped that, should the chest grab the attention of kind passersby, they might feed my companion something... help it live on. That's enough.
I know you must feel cheated right now. You might even be furious.
You can insult me however you like, because I really am a despicable bastard, a rat skulking in the shadows of the sewers, scum that isn't fit for the tribe, BUT! Do not tear up this note, and do not move the chest, I beg of you!
By the way, if you're willing, you can leave something in the chest so that the next person to open it won't feel cheated. Both I and my Saurian will be most grateful to you...

imgDesc.text: The settlement of the tribe who live alongside the Yumkasaurs. Their ancestors suspended giant trees here with ropes and grappling hooks, hence the name, "Scions of the Canopy."

Long, long ago, there was an age when the earth refused to accept seeds, when flowers withered and people could no longer turn to the land for sustenance. Instead, the ancestors of that ancient era turned to the gods of night for guidance.
A world born from wall graffiti, or one concealed by expressive writings... Who knows which of these it is?
"O puny people, o power-hungry race — what price are you willing to pay? What sacrifice will you make for that which you covet?"
